Finding: firebase/storage.rules grants unauthenticated public read+write on /uploads /profiles /screensaver /templates; app has no Firebase Auth bridge so request.auth is always null
Evidence: firebase/storage.rules lines 1-29; independently confirmed by 3 of 5 audit tracks (security, download-failures, unpaid-uploads)
Reproduction: Unauthenticated GET/PUT against a known or guessed /uploads/{name}/{timestamp}_{file} path in the Storage emulator with real storage.rules loaded
User_Impact: Any customer document can be read or overwritten by anyone with no account; privacy breach and document-tampering risk
Financial_Impact: High -- customer PDFs/images (potentially sensitive) exposed; overwrite risk on shared templates used by every kiosk job
Recommended_Fix: Build Firebase-Auth custom-token bridge and scope rules by request.auth.uid, or move to short-lived signed URLs for reads and presigned PUT with TTL for writes; remove allow write: if true immediately
Verification_Status: Confirmed Bug (code + rules text read directly, not inferred)

Finding: 24-hour automatic file deletion may not be running in production; code's own docs say not deployed; CI does not auto-deploy the scheduled trigger functions; orphan sweep defaults to dry-run with no override found in repo env files
Evidence: docs/deployment/STORAGE_CLEANUP.md top-of-file status note; .github/workflows/deploy-functions.yml trigger deploy list; commit f6a3d1da documents prior mechanism silently found 0 candidates for 30+ days vs 507 real candidates
Reproduction: Grep functions/.env and functions/.env.production for ORPHAN_CLEANUP_MODE (absent); compare CI_CD.md's live-trigger inventory (dated before the fix) against the fix commit date
User_Impact: Customer documents may remain in storage, publicly readable (see F-01), far longer than the advertised 24 hours, or indefinitely
Financial_Impact: Storage cost growth; compliance/privacy exposure if files are expected to be purged and are not
Recommended_Fix: Run firebase functions:list against production to confirm deployment; deploy via the documented manual opt-in if missing; only then set ORPHAN_CLEANUP_MODE=delete and redeploy
Verification_Status: Unverified -- requires live Firebase project access this audit did not have

Finding: No Firebase Storage signed URLs anywhere in the codebase; document access never expires once the URL/path is known
Evidence: Repo-wide grep for getSignedUrl/signedUrl/generateV4 returns zero hits in functions/ or mimo-website/; getDownloadURL() tokens used instead (perpetual)
Reproduction: Fetch a getDownloadURL() URL for a document days after upload; it still resolves
User_Impact: Customer documents remain accessible indefinitely via an old URL even after the UI stops referencing them
Financial_Impact: Compounds F-01's exposure window
Recommended_Fix: Implement expiring, backend-issued signed URLs for all document reads

Finding: Direct-to-Storage uploads bypass the Express backend entirely -- no size limit, no MIME allowlist, no rate limiting applied to the primary website upload path
Evidence: mimo-website/src/app/pages/upload-file.tsx uploadBytesResumable call; functions/src/middleware/rateLimit.js has no limiter applied to any upload route
Reproduction: Upload an arbitrarily large or arbitrary-type file directly via the Storage SDK without ever calling /finalize-upload
User_Impact: Unlimited anonymous storage consumption; a backend file-type/size check in postFinalizeUpload is advisory only since the object already exists before that call runs
Financial_Impact: Storage cost / quota-exhaustion DoS risk, fully unauthenticated
Recommended_Fix: Add a max file size and MIME allowlist enforced at the Storage-rules layer (not just in the controller) once F-01's auth bridge exists

Finding: postCreateOrder's ownership/status check is a plain read (not a transaction) with a Cashfree network round-trip before the Firestore write; concurrent/retried checkout can create two live orders for the same files
Evidence: functions/src/controllers/payment.controller.js postCreateOrder, lines ~18-457; contrasted with the already-transactional postPaymentSuccess
Reproduction: Static analysis: two near-simultaneous calls to /create-order for the same pending jobIds both pass the pending-status check before either commits
User_Impact: Customer sees duplicate/confusing orders; at most one can be paid, so no double-charge, but a real unpaid Cashfree order record is created
Financial_Impact: Low direct financial impact (unpaid duplicate is not charged) but creates gateway-side clutter and customer confusion
Recommended_Fix: Wrap the ownership/status check and the Firestore batch in a transaction, mirroring the existing fix in postPaymentSuccess
Verification_Status: Confirmed Bug (static analysis only; not dynamically reproduced per the audit's no-live-payment rule)

Finding: /kiosk/report-failure, which triggers a real Cashfree refund via a shared-secret check, has no rate limiting at all
Evidence: functions/src/routes/kiosk.routes.js ~line 430; functions/src/middleware/rateLimit.js's limiter list does not include this route
Reproduction: If the shared INTERNAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET were ever guessed or leaked, nothing throttles repeated refund-trigering calls
User_Impact: Potential for refund abuse if the internal secret is ever compromised
Financial_Impact: Could enable repeated unauthorized refund attempts with no throttle, pending secret compromise
Recommended_Fix: Add a rate limiter to this route matching the pattern already used elsewhere in the file

Finding: Plaintext password logged on every failed admin-login attempt
Evidence: functions/src/controllers/admin.controller.js line 57: console.log of reqPassword and both admin/finance emails on auth failure
Reproduction: Submit an incorrect password to POST /admin/login and inspect Cloud Logging output (not done against production in this audit; confirmed by reading the log statement itself)
User_Impact: A legitimate admin/finance user who mistypes their password leaks a near-real or real password into logs readable by anyone with log access
Financial_Impact: Could lead to credential compromise if logs are exported or broadly accessible
Recommended_Fix: Remove reqPassword (and the real env credential identifiers) from this log line; rotate ADMIN_PASSWORD/FINANCE_PASSWORD as a precaution
Verification_Status: Confirmed Bug (exact line read, value itself not printed per audit rules)

Finding: Generic (non-PDF, non-Office, non-image) upload branch accepts any file type with only a 256-byte minimum floor; no malware/AV scanning anywhere in the pipeline
Evidence: functions/src/controllers/upload.controller.js catch-all branch; contrasted with functions/src/document-scanner/scanner.controller.js's correct MIME allowlist + 10MB cap pattern
Reproduction: Upload an arbitrary binary with an unrecognized extension; it is accepted, billed as 1 page, and a print_jobs doc is created
User_Impact: Malicious or malformed files can enter the pipeline and reach the Office converter or print queue
Financial_Impact: Low-to-medium depending on converter-service robustness (not reviewed in this audit)
Recommended_Fix: Apply the document-scanner's MIME-allowlist + size-cap pattern to the generic upload path; add a basic malware/heuristic scan before conversion or printing

Finding: No rate limiting on /technical/login, /hr/login, /marketing/login, or /google-login
Evidence: functions/src/middleware/rateLimit.js's loginLimiter is applied only to /register /login /guest-session and /admin/login
Reproduction: Repeated POSTs to one of the four unrated login endpoints with no throttling observed in the route definitions
User_Impact: Credential brute-forcing is possible against these four staff-facing login endpoints
Financial_Impact: Depends on password strength of the affected accounts; low-to-medium given presumably low account count
Recommended_Fix: Apply the existing loginLimiter to all four routes

Finding: No rate limiting on /finalize-upload, /create-order, /payment-success, /request-refund, /generate-text-pdf, /create-blank-job
Evidence: functions/src/routes/upload.routes.js and payment.routes.js -- these routes carry only authMiddleware, no limiter
Reproduction: An authenticated or guest session can call these endpoints at unlimited frequency
User_Impact: Cost/DoS risk: a single guest session (trivially obtained via /guest-session) can hammer the Office converter or Cashfree order-creation endpoint
Financial_Impact: Medium -- external API cost exposure (Cloud Run converter, Cashfree order creation) with no backend throttle
Recommended_Fix: Apply a reasonable per-user/per-IP rate limiter to these routes

Finding: WhatsApp payment success handler (getWaPaySuccess) generates and assigns a print code outside any Firestore transaction, unlike the equivalent and already-fixed website path (postPaymentSuccess)
Evidence: functions/src/controllers/whatsapp.controller.js getWaPaySuccess ~lines 73-95, contrasted with payment.controller.js postPaymentSuccess lines 809-894
Reproduction: Two near-simultaneous hits on this endpoint for the same orderId (plausible via Cashfree redirect + manual refresh) could both observe no code yet, both generate a valid code, and race on the final batch.commit(), silently wasting one generated code and potentially sending a stale code over WhatsApp
User_Impact: Customer may receive a print code that does not match what is actually stored on their job
Financial_Impact: Wasted print-code slot (held for 24h); potential customer confusion if the wrong code was already sent
Recommended_Fix: Wrap the check-generate-write sequence in db.runTransaction exactly like postPaymentSuccess already does
Verification_Status: Confirmed Bug (static analysis only; not load-tested due to time budget)

Finding: postGetDocumentsByCode (document-preview endpoint shown before a print is actually triggered) lacks the >1-matching-job fail-loudly guard that the sibling /kiosk/print endpoint already has since a 2026-10-16 fix
Evidence: functions/src/controllers/print.controller.js lines 6-102 (queries status==paid, uses docs[0] with no size check), contrasted with kiosk.routes.js lines ~330-338
Reproduction: If a code-collision between two paid jobs were ever to occur (now largely prevented upstream per the printCode.service.js fix), this endpoint would silently merge or arbitrarily pick between two different customers' document metadata
User_Impact: Filename/page-count metadata of the wrong customer's job could be displayed to the kiosk UI before print-trigger catches the mismatch
Financial_Impact: Low today (upstream collision is prevented); would be higher if the upstream fix were ever regressed
Recommended_Fix: Port the same '>1 paid doc found -> fail loudly (409)' guard from kiosk.routes.js into this endpoint
Verification_Status: Partially Implemented (gap confirmed by code reading)

Finding: No explicit payment-session expiry; Cashfree USER_DROPPED/PAYMENT_FAILED webhook events are acknowledged with no state change, leaving the job pending indefinitely until the unrelated 24h storage-age sweep eventually catches it
Evidence: functions/src/controllers/payment.controller.js lines 733-737 (generic webhook handler, explicit no-op comment)
Reproduction: Trigger a failed/dropped payment webhook (not done against production); confirmed by reading the handler's no-op branch
User_Impact: Abandoned payment sessions are invisible as a distinct state; only resolved indirectly, and only if F-02's cleanup is actually deployed
Financial_Impact: No direct financial impact; operational/data-hygiene gap
Recommended_Fix: Add an explicit failed/expired transition on these webhook events so abandoned jobs can be cleaned up without waiting the full 24h window

Finding: Print codes are generated with Math.random(), not a cryptographically secure RNG
Evidence: functions/src/services/printCode.service.js line 19
Reproduction: N/A -- code reading only; keyspace and RNG choice confirmed directly in source
User_Impact: Uniqueness is unaffected (enforced at the DB layer independently); unpredictability of a given code relies entirely on rate limiting, not the RNG itself
Financial_Impact: Low direct impact given the compensating rate limiter (5/min, 20/hr); residual risk if rate limiting is ever bypassed or misconfigured
Recommended_Fix: Move to crypto.randomInt(1000, 10000) as defense in depth

Finding: /kiosk/report-clean is missing the fail-closed INTERNAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET-unset guard that its sibling /report-failure already has
Evidence: functions/src/routes/kiosk.routes.js line ~628 (secretsMatch(secret, process.env.INTERNAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET) with no explicit unset check), contrasted with report-failure's explicit guard at line ~433
Reproduction: If INTERNAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET is ever unset/empty in a deployment, secretsMatch(undefined, undefined) both hash to sha256('') and return true, bypassing auth entirely
User_Impact: Low -- this endpoint only writes a maintenance-log doc and sends an internal email, no refund/financial action
Financial_Impact: Low; requires a specific misconfiguration (unset env var) to be exploitable
Recommended_Fix: Add the same explicit !process.env.INTERNAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET guard that report-failure already has

Finding: /payment-success route is sent an internalSecret by its two legitimate internal callers, but the endpoint itself never reads or validates that field -- dead security control
Evidence: functions/src/controllers/payment.controller.js postPaymentSuccess, full 798-969 body read, no reference to req.body.internalSecret found; functions/src/routes/payment.routes.js line 16 shows the route behind authMiddleware only
Reproduction: N/A -- static code analysis; confirmed the field is sent by callers (getVerifyPayment, webhook handler) but never checked in the handler itself
User_Impact: Not currently exploitable -- the real gate (server-side PAID-status verification) is independent and fails closed on its own
Financial_Impact: None currently, since the real protection is elsewhere
Recommended_Fix: Either enforce internalSecret as a genuine check or remove it and the misleading 'internal' framing/comment
Verification_Status: Partially Implemented (dead code, confirmed by full-file read)

Finding: Customer email addresses and generated/converted file URLs appear in debug log statements
Evidence: functions/src/controllers/payment.controller.js lines ~389,922 ([EMAIL-DEBUG] logs userEmail); functions/src/controllers/upload.controller.js line ~145 (logs printable file URL)
Reproduction: N/A -- code read directly; log statements confirmed present
User_Impact: Minor PII exposure to anyone with log access; file URLs don't add material new exposure given F-01's already-public bucket
Financial_Impact: Low
Recommended_Fix: Remove or redact PII from debug log statements; avoid logging full document URLs

Finding: Storage upload path is keyed by sanitized display name (not user ID) plus millisecond timestamp, so two accounts with the same display name can collide into the same folder; no content-hash or generation-match guard on writes
Evidence: mimo-website/src/app/pages/upload-file.tsx lines ~579-580
Reproduction: Two scripted uploads with the same sanitized username and identical millisecond timestamp overwrite each other (not reproduced against production; reasoned from the path-construction code)
User_Impact: Rare in practice (millisecond-timestamp collision is very unlikely) but structurally possible; combined with F-01's public write, becomes attacker-controllable rather than purely accidental
Financial_Impact: Low on its own; elevated when combined with F-01
Recommended_Fix: Key storage paths by user ID (not display name) and/or add a UUID component; add generation-match preconditions on writes
Verification_Status: Partially Implemented (weak collision resistance, not a confirmed exploited bug)

Finding: CORS configured with origin: true (fully reflective) on the backend API
Evidence: functions/src/server.js line 10
Reproduction: N/A
User_Impact: Standard practice for a bearer-token API where cookies aren't used for auth; not a vulnerability on its own in this architecture
Financial_Impact: None
Recommended_Fix: No action required; documented as a deliberate, reasonable choice for this auth model

Finding: WA_VERIFY_TOKEN has a hardcoded non-secret fallback value
Evidence: functions/src/config/env.js line ~14, with an in-code console.warn already referencing this as a known, non-critical issue
Reproduction: N/A
User_Impact: None -- this token is only used for Meta's one-time webhook-verification GET handshake; the actual webhook signature check uses a separate secret (WA_APP_SECRET) with no fallback
Financial_Impact: None
Recommended_Fix: Already flagged in-code by the team; no new action needed beyond what's already tracked
